name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_MCQ_Q01 - Sequence of root tip regions from apex upwards

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following regions of a typical root-tip in the correct sequential order starting from the distal apex (tip) and moving proximally upward toward the base of the stem:

(i) Region of maturation
(ii) Root cap
(iii) Region of elongation
(iv) Region of meristematic activity

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A growing root-tip is organised into distinct developmental zones from its protected tip upwards, reflecting cell division, cell enlargement, and cell differentiation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Sequential Order
1. At the extreme apex, the root is covered by the thimble-like root cap, which protects the tender tip as it penetrates the soil.
2. A few millimetres above the root cap lies the region of meristematic activity, consisting of small, thin-walled, rapidly dividing cells with dense protoplasm.
3. Proximal to the meristematic zone is the region of elongation, where cells undergo rapid elongation and enlargement to increase root length.
4. Proximal to the elongation zone is the region of maturation, where cells differentiate and epidermal cells form delicate root hairs.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct sequence from the apex upwards is Root cap \(\rightarrow\) Region of meristematic activity \(\rightarrow\) Region of elongation \(\rightarrow\) Region of maturation, which corresponds to (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (iii) \(\rightarrow\) (i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_MCQ_Q02 - Sequence of semi-technical description of a flowering plant

questiontext.text:
In the semi-technical description of a typical flowering plant, arrange the following components in the standard sequence in which they are presented:

(i) Floral characters (inflorescence and flower parts)
(ii) Habit of the plant
(iii) Floral diagram and floral formula
(iv) Vegetative characters (roots, stem, and leaves)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A semi-technical description of a flowering plant uses brief, scientific terminology presented in a standardised sequence from general external form to summarised floral notation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Sequential Order
1. The description begins with the overall habit of the plant (such as herb, shrub, or tree).
2. Next, the vegetative characters—roots, stem, and leaves—are described.
3. Following vegetative features, the floral characters, including inflorescence and individual flower parts, are detailed.
4. Finally, after describing the various plant parts, a floral diagram and a floral formula are presented to summarise the floral structure.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The proper sequence is Habit of the plant \(\rightarrow\) Vegetative characters \(\rightarrow\) Floral characters \(\rightarrow\) Floral diagram and floral formula, corresponding to (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (i) \(\rightarrow\) (iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_MCQ_Q03 - Order of floral structures in papilionaceous flower from outermost to innermost

questiontext.text:
In a papilionaceous flower of family Fabaceae (such as Pisum sativum), arrange the following floral structures in the correct order from the outermost/posterior overlapping structure inward to the enclosed reproductive organs:

(i) Two anterior keel petals
(ii) Diadelphous stamens and monocarpellary pistil
(iii) Largest posterior standard petal
(iv) Two lateral wing petals

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Flowers of family Fabaceae exhibit a characteristic papilionaceous corolla with vexillary aestivation, in which petals are arranged in a specific overlapping hierarchy from posterior to anterior, enclosing the essential reproductive whorls.

Step 2: Evaluation of Sequential Order
1. The outermost and largest petal is the posterior standard, which overlaps the petals beside it.
2. Immediately internal to the standard are the two lateral wing petals, which are overlapped by the standard and in turn overlap the anterior petals.
3. Inside the wings lie the two smallest anterior petals fused/forming a keel.
4. The keel directly encloses the essential reproductive organs, namely the diadelphous stamens and monocarpellary pistil.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Moving from the outermost overlapping petal inward to the enclosed reproductive structures, the correct sequence is Posterior standard \(\rightarrow\) Two lateral wings \(\rightarrow\) Two anterior keel petals \(\rightarrow\) Diadelphous stamens and monocarpellary pistil, which corresponds to (iii) \(\rightarrow\) (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (i) \(\rightarrow\) (ii).
